Order 
01. With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

02. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant / claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 30.1.2015 passed in MACC No.77/2013 by the XIV Addl. Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.5,75,071/- has been awarded to the appellant / claimant by way of compensation.
03. Short facts of the case are that on 10.2.2013 at about 1.30 PM the appellant Baskarbee was travelling to Dewas on motorcycle with her husband.

When she reached in front of Best Price bypass, Indore at that time, the driver/respondent No.2 of truck bearing registration No.HR 55/F-5550 (owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.3) driving the insured vehicle rashly and negligently, dashed the motorcycle of the appellant from behind because of which appellant sustained grievous injuries.
She was admitted in the hospital, but eventually died during treatment.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:31853 2 MA-813-2015 03.
Thereafter the appellant filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 for award of compensation to her on account of injuries sustained.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal concluded that the insured vehicle Baskar Bee vs Heavy Cargo Movers India Pvt. Ltd. on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75874975/
1 caused the accident due to its rash and negligent driving and has awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,75,071/-.

sentences.text: However out of this total compensation, an amount of Rs.4,82,471/- was for expenditure incurred in the tratement of the appellant.
04. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that after this amount is excluded there is a meager amount of compensation for grievous injuries sustained by her.
He submits that medical expert.

Dr.
Ashish Mehrotra (AW2) before the tribunal, proved the permanent disability certificate Exhibit P/9 and stated that the appellant has suffered 40% permanent disability into her lower limb.
He also points out that the appellant underwent plastic surgery.
She has been implanted upon with a rod in her left lower limb.
She also suffered lesions in her hip and knee joints.
The medical expert before the tribunal certified 20% over all disability.

However the tribunal has reduced the same to 10%
without there being any justification to it.
He further submits that the income of the appellant was taken by the claims tribunal at Rs.3000/- per month in terms of findings recorded in para 16.
However even if the appellant is considered as a housewife still her income could not have been taken below the minimum wages prescribed for an unskilled labourer at the relevant time.

He further submits that in other heads also meager amount has been awarded for example for special diet Rs.5000/-, for transportation Rs.3000/- and for attendant Rs.3000/- has been awarded which is very meager looking to the prolonged treatment which has been taken by the appellant which in fact still continuing.

He further refers to the application filed under Order 41 Rule 27 of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:31853 3 MA-813-2015 CPC vide I.A.No.5628/2015,
and submits that even after passing of the award the treatment continued which is demonstrated by way of documents pointed out by the aforesaid application filed before this Court.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation under various heads.

05. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Co. submits that claims tribunal has carefully gone through the record and after calculating the entire expenditure in her treatment awarded the compensation.
The medical expenditure has been reimbursed in full.
He also submits that fracture of left lower limb has now been united which is admitted by medical expert himself.
As such, there is no requirement for enhancement of compensation and appeal deserves to be dismissed.

06. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
07.

From the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 18 it would come to the fore that after accident on 10.2.2013 the appellant had to remain hospitalized at Mayur hospital, Indore up to the period of 13.3.2013 ie., for a period of 3 months and one day which show the gravity of injury sustained by the appellant in the accident.
It has also been seen that she had not only been operated upon but implant of rod was inserted in her left lower limb.
She has to undergo plastic surgery.
Still the wound in her left lower limb refuses to heal.
She is still under treatment for that wound.

Considering the same if the amount of medical expenditure excluded from the total sum of compensation then the compensation for injury is only Rs.90,000/-, which is much less than what should be awarded.
In view of the injuries sustained by the appellant.
This Court is of the considered view that if in the circumstances of the present case a further lump sum amount of Rs.3,00,000/- is awarded then it will constitute just compensation.

Hence it is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:31853 4 MA-813-2015 directed that the appellant shall be entitled to receive Baskar Bee vs Heavy Cargo Movers India Pvt. Ltd. on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75874975/
2 Rs.3,00,000/- as compensation over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal,
which shall carry the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition before the claims tribunal.
08.
